library_note: There is no kitchen-and-bath reference library yet. The `owl` template reference (https://owlroofing.com/, role: primary) supplies the STRUCTURE — it is trade-agnostic. Brand tokens below come entirely from the client's own Elementor global tokens, not from any reference URL. No Firecrawl spend on reference URLs this run.

references.used_for: fixed section order and component set only — never copy program names or copy

brand_source.fonts: Google Fonts link on morriskitchensllc.com — Archivo (300, 400)
brand_source.colors: Elementor global tokens in /wp-content/uploads/elementor/css/post-7.css — primary #114261, secondary #FFFFFF, text #000000, accent #9CC233

rationale: The client's brand is a deep navy (#114261) paired with a lime green (#9CC233) and set in Archivo. Navy becomes --color-primary and drives the dark bands (Testimonials, ProcessSteps, WhyChooseUs, hero scrim); lime becomes --color-accent for fills and buttons. Lime as foreground TEXT on the light background measures only ~1.9:1, so a darkened olive (#4f6b13) is derived for eyebrows, ticks, stars, and chevrons per the owl template's accent-ink rule. The page background moves off pure white to a cool near-white (#f4f6f8) so white surface cards separate — kitchen and bath photography is bright and needs a background that isn't competing with it.
anti_patterns: generic stock photography — this client has ~45 real project photos, use those
Lucide icon rows (max 1 outline icon per section, semantic only)
"Trusted by 10,000+ customers" without a real number from GBP
randomized section order — always use the fixed order from the template
any reuse of Owl Roofing program names ("We Give A Hoot", "Protect Your Nest", "Get It Right Guarantee")
carrying over the client's existing site's slider hero, Elementor layout, or its 'Artisan design team' boilerplate
